about.heading: More than a manufacturer.
paragraphs: Strategic Trust for Advanced and Reliable Knowledge (STARK) is a Saudi manufacturer of integrated environments: woodworks, furniture and mattresses.

We are more than a manufacturer: a trusted solutions partner that brings design, manufacturing, and on-site execution into a single, accountable process. Every piece is engineered for durability and finished to a standard that hospitality demands.
From bespoke wood elements and full interior fit-outs to comfort-engineered mattresses, our work is built to last and made to measure, with fair, quality-first practices at every stage.

process.heading: Our Process
process.sub: From first drawing to final handover: four considered steps behind every project we deliver.

steps.title: Design
steps.body: We shape each piece around the space and the brief, balancing form, function, and proportion.

steps.title: Source
steps.body: Responsibly sourced solid hardwoods and materials, selected for durability and finish.

steps.title: Craft
steps.body: Our workshop cuts, joins, and finishes every surface to a repeatable production standard.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.body: Coordinated delivery and installation, so your space is ready the moment it arrives.

turnkey.heading: Design, manufacture, deliver and install.
turnkey.sub: Most projects are assembled from four suppliers and one long argument about whose fault it is. STARK is built to remove that argument: one company, one contract, one standard, one name on the outcome.

features.title: One accountable partner
features.body: Design, production and site work sit under a single contract, so nothing falls into a gap between trades.

features.title: Made to measure
features.body: Every element is drawn for the room it will stand in and built to those dimensions, so the piece fits the space rather than the space being altered to take the piece.

features.title: One quality standard
features.body: The same stage-gated checks apply to a wood element, a piece of furniture and a mattress.

features.title: Delivered, not shipped
features.body: Coordinated delivery and installation. The project ends when the space is ready, not when the truck leaves.

hero.sub: STARK's woodworks division takes a project from raw panel to installed interior: engineered joinery, fitted furniture and full interior fit-outs, produced on our own lines and installed by our own teams.
hero.alt: Machined timber on the production line.

capabilities.heading: Built like a factory, finished like a workshop.
capabilities.sub: Volume production and bespoke joinery are usually different businesses. Running both on the same lines is what lets a single project keep one standard from the lobby to the last guest room.

items.title: Automated production lines
items.body: Panel processing, edge work and boring run on programmed equipment, so the four-hundredth component matches the first. Repeatability is what makes a large fit-out possible without a drop in finish.

items.title: Engineered tolerances
items.body: Components are cut to a specified tolerance rather than to a fitter's judgement on site, which is why our assemblies close cleanly against walls that are never quite square.

items.title: Finishing in-house
items.body: Spray, lacquer and hand finishing happen under our roof, on our schedule. Nothing waits in a queue at a third-party shop, and nothing arrives on site with a finish nobody signed off.

services.heading: Integrated solutions, delivered end to end.
services.sub: Most interiors are assembled from separate suppliers who each own a piece and none of the outcome. These sit under one name.

items.title: Turnkey Projects

materials.heading: Specified, not improvised.
materials.sub: Substrate and finish are chosen against how a surface will actually be used (humidity, traffic, cleaning regime) and recorded so a repair in year five matches the original.

items.label: Engineered panel
items.body: Dimensionally stable substrates for large flat surfaces that must stay flat.

items.label: Solid hardwood
items.body: Where an edge will be touched, seen close, or has to take a knock.

items.label: Veneer
items.body: Book-matched and sequenced across a run so a wall reads as one piece.

items.label: Laminate & HPL
items.body: High-traffic and wet areas where the cleaning regime is unforgiving.

items.label: Lacquer & PU
items.body: Sprayed finishes, matched to a specified sheen rather than an approximate one.

items.label: Hardware
items.body: Specified to a cycle rating, because the hinge is what fails first on a cheap job.

hero.sub: STARK manufactures mattresses for two very different customers, through two focused brands: one built for the home, one built for hotels that replace a floor at a time.
hero.alt: Finished bedroom interior with a STARK mattress.

brands.heading: One factory, two very different buyers.
brands.sub: A family choosing a bed once a decade and a hotel replacing two hundred of them need different products, different warranties and different conversations. Pretending otherwise is how one of them ends up badly served.

items.name: blue mattress
items.body: Spring and foam mattresses designed for modern homes and everyday rest, with the construction explained rather than hidden behind a marketing name.
items.alt: Bedroom with a blue mattress product.

items.name: siesta mattresses
items.body: Durable, high-performance mattresses engineered to hotel and resort standards, consistent across a large order and delivered against a programme rather than a promise.

engineering.heading: What is actually inside.
engineering.sub: A mattress is a stack of decisions about support, pressure and heat. These are the ones we make deliberately.

items.title: Support layer
items.body: The part that decides whether your spine stays in line. Specified against the sleeper's weight range rather than a single 'medium' that suits nobody in particular.

items.title: Comfort layer
items.body: Where pressure at the shoulder and hip is dealt with. Too little and you feel the support layer; too much and you sink into it.

items.title: Airflow
items.body: Heat is the most common reason people stop liking a mattress they once loved. Structure and cover are chosen to move it away rather than trap it.

items.title: Edge and cover
items.body: The edge decides whether the usable area matches the size on the label. The cover decides how it survives being cleaned.

credentials.heading: Made here, to a stated standard.
credentials.sub: The claims a manufacturer can actually make. Certifications and figures are confirmed per specification rather than asserted on a web page.

items.title: Own production
items.body: Made on our own lines in the Kingdom, not assembled from imported finished goods with a label applied.

items.title: Material traceability
items.body: Foam, spring and textile inputs are specified and recorded, so a contract order is repeatable and a warranty claim is answerable.

items.title: Batch consistency
items.body: A two-hundred-unit hotel order has to be the same mattress two hundred times. That is a production discipline, not a promise.

items.title: Testing
items.body: Durability and firmness verified against the specification a project was sold on, before it ships.

turnkey.heading: The rest of the room, too.
turnkey.sub: Most hospitality buyers are not just buying beds. STARK's woodworks and fit-out divisions deliver the rest of the room under the same contract.
